approachQuestion.prompt: A monitoring service records one integer reading per minute. For each minute, report how many minutes pass until the first later reading that is strictly higher. If no later reading is higher, report 0 for that minute. Return an array with one answer per input position.
constraints: The immutable array readings has 1 to 200,000 signed 32-bit integers.
Output has exactly n integers, in the same positional order; input and output arrays are excluded from auxiliary space.
A later reading must be strictly greater; equal readings do not qualify.
Use a unit-cost model where reading and index values occupy one machine word.

options.text: Scan left to right. Keep indices whose answer is still unknown; when the current value is higher than the value at the top index, fill that index's wait and continue resolving qualifying top indices, then store the current index.
options.feedback: Each current reading is the first later qualifying reading for every unresolved top position it exceeds; positions are resolved in chronological order.

options.text: For each minute, scan later readings until finding the first strictly higher one, then record the distance or 0.
options.feedback: This gives the right answers, but can rescan the same suffix for many minutes. For a long non-increasing array, the repeated searches do quadratic work.

options.text: Compare each reading only with the immediately following reading; record 1 if it is higher and 0 otherwise.
options.feedback: A qualifying reading can occur several minutes later. For [4, 2, 5], the first answer is 2, not 0.

options.text: Sort a copy of the readings and use the next larger sorted value to determine each wait.
options.feedback: Sorting removes the time order, and equal values or duplicate positions do not identify the first later minute. For [5, 1, 4], the answer for the first position is 0, not a wait to 1.

feedback.reason: The method keeps only unresolved positions whose answer has not yet appeared; a new value settles the positions it qualifies for.
details: Read positions in order and keep unresolved indices. When a new reading exceeds the reading at the most recent unresolved index, record the distance for that index and remove it; repeat while the top qualifies. Then add the current index. Any indices still present at the end keep answer 0.

Unresolved indices wait for a strictly greater later value. Equal readings do not resolve each other. Store indices, not just values, because the answer is a distance; unresolved final indices retain zero.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for resolve-waiting-indices. Let n be the number of readings. The input readings and returned answer array are excluded from auxiliary space.
constraints: Each index is pushed once and removed at most once. A reading/index pair occupies a constant number of words.
The scan stops after processing all readings. The output array is required by the problem and excluded.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Every unresolved index is pushed once and removed at most once.
details: Each index enters the unresolved collection once and leaves it at most once, although several removals may happen during one reading. The auxiliary collection can contain n indices; the required answer array is excluded.
